description: A clock divider with eight outputs, each on its own ratio, and a control voltage that rotates which ratio each output carries

params.text: One of the six jumpers on the circuit board; installed, the outputs count down-beat and all eight fire on the first clock pulse. Removed, they count up-beat, each firing after its own count
One of the six jumpers; installed, the outputs hold a gate that changes state on each count. Removed, they send a short trigger
One of the six jumpers, and one of the two that set the largest divider between them: with both installed the largest is 8, with both removed 64, and with this one alone removed 32
One of the six jumpers, and one of the two that set the largest divider between them: with both installed the largest is 8, with both removed 64, and with this one alone removed 16
One of the six jumpers; installed, the dividers are spread across the whole range the two Max Div jumpers allow instead of bunching at the low end
One of the six jumpers; installed, the module resets itself every time twice the largest divider has been counted, which brings odd dividers back into step

inputs.text: A steady voltage from 0V to 5V rotates the table, moving every output onto a different ratio; negative voltages and an unpatched jack count as 0V, and anything above 5V counts as 5V
A rising edge above 3.5V restarts the count on every output; the jack rearms below 0.2V
The clock every output divides, counted on a rising edge above 3.5V and rearmed below 0.2V; with nothing patched here all eight displays read two dashes and the lamp by RESET turns red

outputs.text: A 5V trigger or gate at the ratio the display beside it shows

notes: the six jumpers are hidden until you tick Access jumpers (located on PCB) in the right-click menu, which turns the panel into a circuit board; the panel shows nothing of them otherwise
the module does nothing at all until a clock is patched into CLK
the two-digit display beside each output jack shows that output's current divider and follows the rotation as it changes
the lamp beside the RESET jack is red when no clock is patched, orange on a reset arriving at the jack, and blue on a reset the module gave itself
the Max Div and Spread jumpers apply only to the Manufacturer table; the other four tables ignore them
with Max Div at 8 and Spread installed the largest divider becomes 16 and the eight ratios come out as triplets and sixteenths, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 16
a BRK expander placed against either side of this module drives these six jumpers from switches, so the circuit board never has to be opened
menu: Access jumpers (located on PCB) — swaps the panel for a view of the circuit board, where the six jumpers can be clicked
Dividers table: Manufacturer, Prime numbers, Perfect squares, Fibonacci sequence, Triplet & 16ths — chooses the eight ratios the outputs start from
